content.text: The migrated file still pulls in `dpct/dpct.hpp` and uses `dpct::` helpers and an nd_item-by-hand shim. I'm rewriting it with plain SYCL 2020: a default queue, `sycl::malloc_device`/`sycl::free`, and a 1-D `nd_range` with the same layer guard.

input.summary: Ported matrix_rotate.cu to plain SYCL 2020 (migrated/matrix_rotate.dp.cpp). The migrated file had dpct helpers (dpct/dpct.hpp, dpct::get_current_device, dpct::dpct_free, nd_item shims); I removed all of them. The port now uses sycl::queue (in-order), sycl::malloc_device/sycl::free, q.memcpy, and a 1-D nd_range<1> with a 256-wide work-group and a layer < n/2 guard. The ring-rotation loop body is unchanged from the CUDA kernel. It compiles with icpx -fsycl with zero diagnostics and with add_dpct_include=false, so no dpct headers are needed. Caveat: I have no run/verify tool, so I did not execute the binary or compare its output to the reference. The arithmetic is identical and the in-order queue keeps the repeated launches sequential, so output should match exactly, but exact-match against the reference is not demonstrated.
